how_to_read: open ../../figures/<id>/print.png (or preview.png) and manifest.json; star = must-see; these are references to strengthen a layout derived from your figure's own needs -- borrow the device that serves it, never the layout wholesale

exemplars.why_chosen: One hub state radiates three numbered guarded transitions to peer actions and back to itself; the same hub-and-spoke shape reappears, smaller, nested inside one peer state as its own sub-loop.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put the shared hub state at the centre with peer actions fanning out on numbered, guarded arrows that all loop back to it; draw one action's internal loop as a smaller copy of that exact hub-and-spoke shape inside its box.

exemplars.why_chosen: Splitting the cold-page state in two, with and without a remembered swap-entry, lets Canvas make repeated swap-outs lock-free instead of reallocating an entry every time.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Keep the node small (a digit), put the state's name outside it as a heading, guards in italic on curved arrows

exemplars.why_chosen: A start/end pseudo-state pair brackets three parallel classify-then-act branches, so a control loop with three different action paths still reads as one left-to-right pass.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Bracket the loop with dashed start/end pseudo-states; fan out from start into parallel same-shaped classification branches, one per case, each running its own action box before rejoining the end state and looping back to start.

exemplars.why_chosen: CCF extends Raft's Follower/Candidate/Leader state machine with a Joiner bootstrapping state and two protocol extensions, CheckQuorum (a leader steps down without a quorum) and ProposeVote (a retiring leader fast-tracks a successor), drawn as dashed additions over Raft's solid original states and transitions.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Solid = the known protocol, dashed = this paper's addition, for both nodes and edges; circle only the transitions the text discusses

exemplars.why_chosen: Numbers three pipeline stages that repeat one 'history feeds a state-checker with a red terminal outcome' template for value and for frequency, then merges both verdicts in the third stage.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Repeat one small template, a running history feeding a state-checker box with a red terminal outcome, once for the traced value and once for its frequency; number both ①② and combine their verdicts in a third numbered checker.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two stacked yes/no diamonds whose NO branches both dead-end in one shared fallback box, while YES keeps narrowing to a specific pick — logic collapsed to its actual branch count.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Chain the diamonds vertically and route every NO arrow into one shared fallback box instead of a separate box per branch, then tie the flowchart to the candidate-pool icon cluster with a single bracket leader line, not repeated arrows.

exemplars.why_chosen: A monitoring-loop flowchart where each stage box shows its own literal example buffer (coloured D/O event tiles) feeding a yes/no gate that self-loops until enough events accumulate.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Put a real buffer of coloured event tiles inside each box, and loop its gate diamond back into that box on 'no' but forward to the next box on 'yes' — but three stacked diamonds stay dense to trace.

exemplars.why_chosen: Read-delegation and write-combining share one twin-diamond decision skeleton; a green 'Time Window' bracket marks the one real memory round-trip that queued duplicate requests reuse instead of repeating it.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Bracket the delegate's one memory round-trip as a 'Time Window,' with dashed arrows fanning back to queued duplicate requests instead of repeating the trip; draw the bypass path looping visibly under every memory-side phase box.

exemplars.why_chosen: One inconsistency verdict, computed once at a Handler node, is re-stamped with the same two accent colours and Prioritize/Abort labels at three completely different scheduler layers below.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Compute the verdict once at the top and re-draw its two accent colours plus Prioritize/Abort text at every layer below, even as each layer's queue icon changes shape — but reused bare letters force reading by position, not name.

exemplars.why_chosen: A token-bucket flowchart where every box's role (component / condition / action) is readable from one shared shape+colour code alone, with database cylinders hanging off the chain as side-cars.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Give every box one of three shape+colour roles (blue rounded = component, violet diamond = condition, tan dashed = action), and feed each side-car database with a dashed 'Update' arrow kept separate from its plain read arrow.

exemplars.why_chosen: A registration timeline sets up vCPU-as-CPU, then one decision-diamond template — with the same little CPU-state lookup table inside — is reused twice for source and destination routing.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Embed the literal small state-lookup table inside the decision diamond itself, reuse that exact diamond+table shape for both the source and destination check, and bracket the two halves in one accent colour to name the phases.

exemplars.why_chosen: STRAW tracks a read counter per block and per wordline; every interval it checks each wordline's accumulated disturbance against a threshold, relocates the valid pages of any heavily-disturbed wordline, and erases the block once nothing valid remains.
exemplars.what_to_learn: One fill colour per functional stage; `Y`/`N` on every branch; a labelled loop box containing its own decision

exemplars.why_chosen: PIPM extends MSI cache coherence with two migration-aware states (ME, I') encoded via directory state plus an in-memory bit, adding six new host/device transitions.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a directory-state-plus-status-bit truth table paired with a circle-and-arrow state diagram sharing the same state names

exemplars.why_chosen: Four-panel figure where a numbered synthesis pipeline (with a feedback loop) sits beside the resulting protocol trace and the two original protocols it fuses, using one shared sequence-diagram notation throughout.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw the synthesized protocol and both source protocols with the same lifeline-plus-boxed-state notation so states and messages line up panel to panel, and carry one two-colour domain tint through every panel.

exemplars.why_chosen: A CPU-triggered write to DATA is checked by hardware against STATUS::FULL to decide whether the queue moves to Busy or QueueFull; RESET forces Idle from anywhere, and CONFIG may only be touched while Idle.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a two-colour solid/dashed arrow convention distinguishing software-triggered from hardware-triggered transitions; a nested dotted substate box inside a solid superstate box to show refinement without adding a new top-level state; a small legend box inside the diagram itself explaining the arrow-colour convention

exemplars.why_chosen: Reaching a later chunk of video 2 requires surviving one independent swipe-away decision at every intervening chunk, each with its own probability.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a repeating continue-or-branch-off decision unit chained left to right to build a recursive probability model

exemplars.why_chosen: A page fault takes one of three shortcuts depending on cache and memory state, but every path converges on the same metadata-update and PTE-install finish, with only two steps needing locks.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Long bypass arrows over the top for fast paths; an icon + fill + legend marking the steps that need locks

exemplars.why_chosen: RAPID's blocking mode is a 4-state FSM (Run, Wait, Suspend, Schedule) driven by the packet buffer PB: a flow is suspended whenever PB is non-empty and only returns to normal Run processing once a timeout finds PB empty after scheduling.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a small colour-coded finite-state machine with one accent colour per state and its adjoining transitions

exemplars.why_chosen: MetaOpt avoids needlessly rewriting an inner problem: if aligned with the outer objective or merely a feasibility problem, its constraints are merged in as is; otherwise a convex problem gets a primal-dual/KKT rewrite, and anything else is marked NA.
exemplars.what_to_learn: A left-to-right diamond cascade: `Y` drops to a terminal box, `N` continues right, so the unhandled case lands last

exemplars.why_chosen: Practitioners can pick a suitable max-min fair allocator with two questions: whether a strict fairness guarantee is required (routing to GB), and if not, which pair of properties they prioritize, each routing to a different named allocator and parameter.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Colour only the leaves; leave decision nodes unfilled; write branch conditions as full words on the edge

exemplars.why_chosen: To build a positive test case exercising DFA state 5, MESSI concatenates two paths: P1 (1→3→5) from the start to the target state, and P2 (5→7→9→10) from the target onward to an accepting state.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a plain state-machine diagram with two differently-styled highlighted paths stitched together at a shared target state to build one worked example

exemplars.why_chosen: A single decision tree, split into four subsystem lanes, cascades Z-score threshold checks so the metrics closest to the root are the ones most sensitive to a faulty machine.
exemplars.what_to_learn: repeated check-node cascade (low: next check, high: verdict leaf), grouped into lanes by subsystem

exemplars.why_chosen: All studied systems detect slowness the same two-staged way: a monitored metric first crosses a warning threshold, triggering a warning action, and only reaches a fatal action either by exceeding a separate, higher fatal threshold directly, or by accumulating enough warnings (the warning count) over time.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a two-threshold decision flowchart generalized from many concrete systems' logic, with a small reference table of real threshold values alongside it

exemplars.why_chosen: The same two naturally-consistent transactions that dOCC's locking validation falsely aborts under contention are both committed by NCC's timestamp pre-assignment, refinement, and safeguard check, with a middle panel showing how per-version timestamps get refined.
exemplars.what_to_learn: swimlane timelines for two clients and the keys they touch, with per-client colour coding kept consistent across a 'before' and 'after' panel to highlight a protocol fix

exemplars.why_chosen: Only memory that is Locked, VMPL0-private and content-verified may be treated as memory-safe; sharing, copying or writing are the sole safe ways to move between the five permission states.
exemplars.what_to_learn: small badge-icon pairs (trust glyph + lock glyph) attached to each named state of an access-permission state machine

exemplars.why_chosen: Two identical page-state-machine templates side by side (state spine + numbered steps + linked epoch-phase column), differing only by one extra intermediate state and its numbering.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Draw each variant as an identical spine of numbered states with a phase column linked by short cross-arrows and a return loop on the left; give the busier variant one extra spine state and renumber after it.

exemplars.why_chosen: Two per-slot flags, occupied and complete, define four states - clean, being filled, valid, and invalidated-while-filling - and the Fill/Lock/Invalidate/Evict transitions between them let Scalio detect the race where a slot is invalidated while still being filled.
exemplars.what_to_learn: Four states as one repeated record layout in a 2×2 grid; the flag bits inside are what distinguishes them

exemplars.why_chosen: A cache block's Inactive/Semiactive/Active state, driven purely by whether its CET index and thread reference map (rmap) are set, lets CaM manage concurrent access without locking or unnecessary cache replacement.
exemplars.what_to_learn: The concrete data structure and the abstract machine side by side, sharing one colour key

exemplars.why_chosen: A single per-page survival-ratio threshold, set at the point where the cost curves of remapping and copying cross, is enough to route each page to whichever of the two movement strategies is cheaper.
exemplars.what_to_learn: a central decision diamond routing two colour-coded inputs to two colour-coded strategy boxes, paired with a small inset curve that motivates the decision threshold

exemplars.why_chosen: RT builds a squeeze transducer for one concrete input DFA by taking their automaton product state by state, then projects that product onto its output symbols alone to get the result NFA.
exemplars.what_to_learn: small automaton diagrams whose accepting states are drawn as double circles and whose transitions are labelled input/output pairs; a 2x2 progression from two small input automata to their product and then to a simplified result automaton

exemplars.why_chosen: A low-level state sequence L0..L6 and a high-level sequence H0..H4 run in parallel, with dashed arrows showing each L state's corresponding H state under refinement.
exemplars.what_to_learn: two parallel horizontal state chains at different abstraction levels linked by dashed many-to-one refinement arrows
